candidate.blueprint_locator: Reduction of Risk Potential — recognize treatment-related complications, perform focused assessments, recognize changes in client condition, and intervene as needed.
candidate.educational_objective: Recognize early upper-extremity lymphedema symptoms after axillary lymph-node dissection and prioritize prompt assessment and comparison of the affected limb rather than delaying evaluation or starting unassessed treatment.

options.A: Assess and compare both arms for swelling and other changes and promptly arrange evaluation for possible lymphedema.
options.B: Reassure the client that heaviness and tightness are expected after axillary surgery and require evaluation only if the swelling becomes severe.
options.C: Encourage immediate heavy resistance exercise with the affected arm before any assessment is completed.
options.D: Assume the symptoms prove lymphedema and begin tight compression wrapping without evaluation or fitting by the healthcare team.

candidate.rationale: A is correct. NCI states that lymph-node removal increases lymphedema risk after breast-cancer treatment and advises clients to report even slight changes such as a heavy, full, or tight feeling and swelling. When an arm is affected, evaluation includes examination and comparison with the other limb; additional testing may be used to evaluate causes of swelling. B is incorrect because early symptoms should be reported rather than dismissed until severe. C is incorrect because exercise should be individualized and safe; new symptoms warrant assessment before an unsupervised heavy program. D is incorrect because symptoms do not establish the diagnosis by themselves and compression garments or wraps should be appropriately selected and taught by the healthcare team or certified lymphedema therapist.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Axillary lymph-node removal increases lymphedema risk; early heaviness, tightness and swelling should be reported and assessed; limb comparison is part of evaluation; exercise and compression should be individualized and appropriately supervised.
